findings.text: the new figure script adds two findings under the repository's declared ruff rule set (C408 here and W292 at the file's last line) and fails ruff format --check, so the commit adds findings on a path it stages, against the repository's rule that a commit adds none.

the release assertions cannot fail on an over-firing consumer check, because a follower that ends on its first tick right after arming satisfies all of them (gone, silent, lock free, successor holds), so a regression that ended a follower whose consumer is alive would leave this gate green; the direction is only partly bounded by the five seconds with a live consumer at tests/test_follow_lifetime.py:279.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against base b52bf914; 5194657a adds the consumer check, its call from _tick and the three loop exits to reckon/cli.py plus the new gate, and de550083 adds the landing comment, the archive section id=s7-orphaned-follower-releases and the figure source, where the archive edit is add-only (62/0) over sections s2, s3 and the three s6 sections and the plan edit is a three-line insertion that leaves plan-version and plan-modified untouched.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names tests/test_orphaned_follower_releases.py, and the test holds each clause as written — RECKON_HOME is a temporary directory inherited by every process it starts (tests/test_orphaned_follower_releases.py:97 and :142), an intermediate parent starts the follower and is killed with SIGKILL (:301), and within ten seconds the test observes the follower gone (:198), its stdout empty (:307), a non-blocking flock taking the registration (:211-223) and a second follower as the holder named by follower_state (:248-265) — with one disclosed substitution, the launch form sys.executable -c "from reckon.cli import main; main()" instead of -m reckon or the console-script path, which I confirmed is forced because the package has no __main__ (python -m reckon reports no module named reckon.__main__).
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is that a follower whose recorded consumer is gone releases its registration and exits silently, and reckon/cli.py:1906-1933 implements exactly this over the record written at reckon/crew/runs.py:1507-1508, ends every loop through the consumer_gone exits at reckon/cli.py:2003, :2034, :2050 and :2062 without yielding anything on that path, so the process falls out to the registration context manager at reckon/crew/runs.py:1577-1580, which drops the advisory lock.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory against the completed run, status complete with commits 5194657a and de550083 at base b52bf914, a negative_control_log whose first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim, and five adjacent failures attributed by id and cause, which I re-read in logs/adjacent-follow.log and confirmed (three state-name expectations such as tests/test_crew_watch_lifetime.py:181 and two from the in-flight attach-line change including the KeyError 'ensure_line' out of crew/node.py, none touching the reviewed diff).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the dispatch fence and the manifest declare reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/runs.py, tests/test_orphaned_follower_releases.py, the evidence archive page, the figure directory and the plan, and git diff --numstat b52bf914..de550083 returns exactly those six entries with reckon/crew/runs.py untouched.

justifications.durability: the gate reddens when the check is deleted (logs/negative-control-consumer-check.log) and every assertion it makes reads a source independent of the code's own report — the process table at tests/test_orphaned_follower_releases.py:198, a fresh non-blocking flock at :213, and the second follower's own recorded pid against the test's own Popen handle at :257 — but it cannot distinguish an over-firing check, because a follower that exits on its first tick right after arming satisfies every observation the test makes, and its real-directory control at :101 re-derives the path by a copy of the production algorithm that matches runs.follower_dir today and would go vacuous silently if the two drift.
justifications.evidence: the gate is the file the done-when names and I re-ran it at the reviewed region of my own tree with the reviewed files byte-identical (1 passed in 8.78 s, EXIT=0, gate-recheck.log), and the control log repeats the declared mutation on its first line and reddens with its own mechanism message, though logs/gate-at-head.log carries no revision, tree or command header and the control never reaches its second clause about follower_state.
justifications.fit: the new names describe their mechanism (_check_consumer, consumer_gone) and carry no plan, sprint or stage label, reckon/cli.py adds no findings (ruff reports the same two under the repository's declared rule set at b52bf914 and at de550083) and the gate is format clean, while the new figure script at docs/figures/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor/orphan_release_timeline.py:89 adds two findings and one format violation.
justifications.goal_fidelity: both clauses of the plan land at reckon/cli.py:1926-1933 (a re-parent shows in os.getppid(), and the recorded start tick is the pid-reuse guard the observer already applies at reckon/crew/runs.py:1893), the silent-exit clause is met by the absence of any yield on the consumer_gone path at reckon/cli.py:2070-2076, and the one gap is the test's follower launch form, disclosed at docs/evidence/archive/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor-landed.html s7 rather than hidden.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --numstat b52bf914..de550083 is exactly the six declared paths with reckon/crew/runs.py declared and untouched, the cumulative archive edit is add-only and leaves the s2, s3 and s6 section ids intact, and the plan edit is a three-line insertion that touches neither plan-version nor plan-modified.
